title: Hierarchical trace sampling controller to cut runtime overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: tracing instrumentation currently adds a measurable CPU and memory tax for high-qps services (notably gateway and routing-proxy). Full-span capture + late tail-based decisions have increased per-request overhead and inflated our storage/ingest costs. Goal: design and roll out a Hierarchical Trace Sampling Controller (HTSC) that minimizes on-path overhead while preserving signal for latency and error investigation.

Approach: implement a two-stage hierarchy: (1) Fast-path probabilistic head-sampling at the instrumented boundary with extremely lightweight metadata (trace_id, brief flags, sampled_hint). Head-sampling reduces capture volume for routine requests with a configurable per-route budget. (2) Independent tail detector/collector that evaluates delayed signals (latency spikes, HTTP 5xx, error breadcrumbs) and requests retroactive enrichment for a bounded set of candidate traces via a low-overhead fetch protocol. A central controller coordinates per-service budgets, emergency boosts (for incidents), and graceful degradation when sidecars/backends are overloaded.

Key design points:
- Per-route sample budgets and time-windowed quotas to avoid p95/spike storms consuming all sampling capacity.
- Lightweight head sample records kept in memory with bounded LRU eviction; no heavy span payloads until final sample decision.
- Tail-detector uses a probabilistic bloom-filter-like shortlist + deterministic rules (status code, latency threshold, percentile outliers) to request full trace shards.
- Safe fallback: when enrichment RPCs fail, head-sampled minimal records remain available for low-fidelity analysis.
- Config driven via console: global default rate, per-service overrides, emergency incident mode (instant boost), and blackout windows for maintenance.

Trade-offs considered:
- Slight complexity increase in sidecars vs. large savings in CPU and storage.
- Potentially delayed visibility for some failure modes until enrichment succeeds; mitigated by keeping lightweight breadcrumbs and structured error logs correlated by trace_id.

Performance targets:
- Reduce trace-related CPU overhead on instrumented paths by >= 35% at p50 on gateway services.
- Decrease emitted span volume by >= 60% overall while retaining >= 95% of high-latency/error traces for debugging.
- No regression of request latency beyond 1ms median added overhead on the fast-path.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement prototype in test sidecar and runtime branch.
2) Bench and load test in staging; gather CPU, memory, and emitted-span metrics.
3) Canary on low-traffic services (internal-api-v1) with telemetry gates for sampling_decision_rate, enrichment_success_rate, and trace_emit_bytes.
4) Gradual ramp to gateway with safety caps and emergency cutoff.

Observability and metrics to add:
- sampling.controller.decisions{route,service,decision} (counter)
- sampling.controller.enrichment_requests_total and enrichment_success_rate (gauge)
- tracing.emit.bytes and tracing.emit.spans (per-service)
- tracing.fastpath.latency_added_ms (histogram)
- alerts: enrichment_success_rate < 90% for 10m, sampling_decisions causing >5% increase in p99 latency

acceptance_criteria: HTSC prototype deployed in staging with head-sampling enabled for gateway-test service
Bench results show >= 35% reduction in tracing CPU overhead at p50 on gateway-test under 1000 qps
Enrichment success metric >= 92% in staging and no increase >1ms median added latency on fast-path
Console controls for per-route budgets visible and editable in a feature-flagged UI
Runbook for incident-mode sampling escalation documented and reviewed
updates: 2025-10-22: Kickoff meeting with runtime, telemetry, and agents teams; agreed on hierarchy and enrichment RPC contract (gRPC proto v1). Action: Miguel to draft proto, Aisha to mock console UX.

2025-10-28: Prototype sidecar implemented (basic head-sampling + in-memory breadcrumb store). Microbench shows head-path allocation drop ~28% vs current full-span capture. Initial review notes: add bounded eviction policy and metrics for dropped breadcrumbs. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4921)

2025-11-02: Load test in staging at 1k qps for gateway-test. Observed tracing CPU down 38%, emitted spans down 62%, enrichment_success_rate 89% (timed out during burst). Action: increase enrichment RPC retry backoff and batch enrichment requests. Filed follow-up ENG-21105 for RPC retry tuning.

2025-11-05: Design review with Security & Privacy: confirmed that breadcrumbs contain no PII and enrichment RPCs respect tenant isolation. Security requested explicit audit log on enrichment requests — added to implementation notes.

2025-11-07: Canary rollout to internal-api-v1 started (10% traffic). Early telemetry: enrichment_success_rate 94%, sampling.controller.decisions shows expected distribution. No observed p99 latency regression. Monitoring dashboards created: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/traces/sampling-overhead
